The Authentic Name

Why krónos.com is the correct form

Greek Original

Κρόνος

The name in its original Greek form. A name that carries the full phonetic weight of its source tradition.

ASCII Constraint

KRONOS

Stripped of its identity, the name was reduced to plain Latin letters. The original orthography — stress, length, breathing — was erased by systems that only understand A-Z.

Unicode Restoration

Krónos

The Unicode restoration recovers what ASCII destroyed. This is philological accuracy — not decoration. The domain encodes to Punycode, but the browser displays the truth.

Valid Scholarly Variations
Kronos krónos Cronus

Each variant is an attested scholarly orthography. The owned form is the active domain; others are historically valid alternatives.

Punycode Encoding
krónos.com → xn--krnos-1ta.com

The non-ASCII characters in Krónos are encoded while the ASCII remains visible. To the DNS, it is Punycode. To humanity, it is Krónos.

Tier Classification

Why Krónos is classified as Tier-2 Accent-Preserving

The Greek original Κρόνος contains only stress (acute accent). This makes it a single-tier Tier-2 name. The Unicode restoration preserves what can be preserved — honoring the single feature that distinguishes it from plain ASCII.

06

Mythology & Lore

The Titan who devoured time

In Hesiod’s Theogony, Krónos is the youngest of the Titans, born from Gaia (Earth) and Ouranos (Sky). Ouranos hated his children and hid them inside Gaia, so Gaia gave Krónos a sickle of adamant and set him against his father.

Krónos castrated Ouranos, separating heaven from earth and taking cosmic kingship. He married his sister Rhea, but a prophecy warned that one of his children would overthrow him. To prevent it, he swallowed each child at birth — Hestia, Demeter, Hera, Hades, and Poseidon.

Rhea hid the youngest, Zeus, in a Cretan cave. When Zeus grew, he forced Krónos to vomit his siblings and led the Olympians in the Titanomachy. Defeated, Krónos was cast into Tartaros — or, in gentler traditions, exiled to the Isles of the Blessed.

07

Pronunciation

How to say the name

Ancient Greek: /kró.nos/ with stress on the first syllable. The omicron is short, so there is no macron.

Modern English usually says KROH-noss. The Unicode restoration Krónos makes the original Greek stress visible — a small but precise piece of philology that plain Kronos erases.

09

Syncretism

Krónos across cultures

Roman Saturn: Krónos was identified with Saturnus, the old god of sowing and seed. His temple at the foot of the Capitoline and the midwinter festival Saturnalia gave Rome one of its most beloved holidays.

Phoenician El: In the Phoenician History of Philo of Byblos, preserved by Eusebius, the Canaanite high god El is explicitly equated with Krónos. Both are the gray-bearded father of the gods, detached from the stormy violence of the younger generation.

Chronos (Time): Later Greek and Roman writers conflated Krónos with the personification of Time, Chronos. The etymology is disputed, but the visual fusion created the familiar image of Father Time with a sickle or scythe.

10

Cultural Legacy

From Titan to Father Time

Krónos gave English “chronic,” “chronology,” and “chronometer” through his later association with time. The planet Saturn bears his Roman name.

In art and folklore he survives as Father Time, the old year yielding to the new. His myth of swallowing children and being overthrown by his son remains one of the great succession narratives of Western culture — a template reused from Hesiod to Romantic poetry to modern fantasy.
